paper_metadata.title: Photoreceiver Module Using an InP HEMT Transimpedance Amplifier for Over 40 Gb/s
paper_metadata.abstract: We developed a photoreceiver module for over 40 Gb/s that uses two ultrahigh-speed device technologies: an InP HEMT transimpedance amplifier (TIA) and a uni-traveling-carrier photodiode (UTC-PD). The TIA was designed to have a wide dynamic range by using cascade HEMT topology for the output buffer. We found that reducing the standing wave at the PD–TIA interface by decreasing the change of arg( 11) of the TIA within the required frequency region is important for increasing the bandwidth of the module. We obtained a minimum sensitivity of 6 dBm and a dynamic range of 11 dB for 43-Gb/s non7 return-to-zero optical input signal. Error-free operation of the module was confirmed at a data rate of 50 Gb/s.
